summary: Carol primes are numbers of the form (2^n − 1)² − 2. The largest known Carol prime remains the one found by Mark Rodenkirch in July 2016 (index n = 695631, 418812 digits, the 44th known Carol prime) — this predates the window and no report of a new record, computational search, or theoretical result (proof, disproof, heuristic density argument, or bound) was found dated after 26 January 2024. OEIS A091516 (list of indices n giving Carol primes) has no comment or data update in the window; the only 2026-dated entry there is a Mathematica code contribution by Harvey P. Dale (9 January 2026), which is a formula/code addition for generating existing terms, not new mathematics or a new prime. Searches for PrimeGrid or other distributed-computing project activity on Carol/Kynea numbers turned up general PrimeGrid records (Mersenne, Generalized Fermat) but nothing Carol-specific in the window. No arXiv paper addressing Carol number primality, density, or infinitude was found. Per §3.1, this is a pure existence/infinitude question ('are there infinitely many'), which per the rules would not be moved by a new example, a record search extended further, or a heuristic density argument alone — it would require an actual proof or disproof, and none exists. Status is therefore open with no_change_found true, and there is no AI involvement of any kind to report.
competing_reading: None found; the question is narrow and specialized enough that a genuine absence of activity is the straightforward reading. The only ambiguity is whether Wikipedia currently maintains a live standalone 'Carol number' article distinct from the general list — a direct fetch of https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carol_number returned a 404 in this session (possibly a transient or redirect issue), but this does not bear on whether any mathematical progress occurred, since mirrors (HandWiki, Wolfram MathWorld, OEIS, Prime-Numbers wiki) were checked and are consistent with each other and with pre-2024 records.
what_would_settle_it: A new largest Carol prime discovered via distributed search (e.g., PrimeGrid) with an announcement dated after 26 January 2024 would show continued computational interest, though would not itself resolve the infinitude question. Only a genuine proof or disproof of infinitude — or a new heuristic/density result specifically about Carol primes published in a paper — would constitute progress under the stated rules.
